Built, measured and refused, and the roadmap already carried the verdict this row did not. exoplasim/notes/non-mpi-performance-roadmap.md section 1: implemented in full, correct, four times smaller (114.9 MB a die to about 36 at T170, 15.1 MB a thread to 4.5, under the 32 MB target) and 1.56% SLOWER on the threaded build at T170 -- 80.57 s against 81.66 s, paired and interleaved, faster in 0 of 4 rounds, [-2.17, -0.74]. The code is reverted; verify_weight_factorisation_model.sh is kept and agreed with the eight-matrix build to 4.8e-13 at one step and 1.06e-11 at twenty against a 1e-10 bar declared before the arms ran.

THE PREMISE WAS BACKWARDS. The route was ranked first because the filter fold returned 1.6%, read as evidence these loops are bound by streaming the weight matrices. Undoing the fold costs the same 1.6% back, and the reading that fits both numbers is that they are bound by the MULTIPLY. A second measurement agrees: at NPRO=1 one thread streams 30 MB of pmat and 30 MB of qmat per transform against 1.88 MB at NPRO=16, and the two time the same, 1.45 ms against 1.48.

SHTns has since removed the matrices altogether, computing the Legendre functions on the fly and storing no NCSP x NLPP array, which takes pmat and qmat out of cache_budget.py entirely. The cache-boundary finding in rank-imbalance-and-weight-traffic.md still stands; what no longer stands is that this is the way to act on it.

Closed WONTFIX. Reopen only if a resolution above T170 makes the memory headroom worth a small speed loss. The row stayed open because a71cc1bc pointed it at the merging worktree and the merge (85de8f85) never reconciled it.

Answered, and by exactly the procedure this row asked for: retaken against the merged build with the cost measured rather than reported. exoplasim/notes/the-zeroing-is-an-init-flag.md carries it.

WHAT THE FLAG WAS WORTH: two T170 threaded binaries from the same source differing in that flag alone, paired and interleaved on the 300-step bed -- 70.55 s with -finit-real=zero against 51.97 s without, +26.03% [+22.76, +27.29], faster in 4 of 4 rounds, and the restart IDENTICAL. Visible statically too: 1193 memset call sites with the flag, 623 without. The cause of the 31% of T170 that shtns-viability.md had attributed to physics routines clearing their own work arrays was the compiler doing it, not the model.

WHETHER THE MODEL NEEDS IT: three gates, and it does not. The trapping gate (-finit-real=snan with -ffpe-trap=invalid) is clean on the legmod path at T21 and T170, at NLOWIO=0 and 1. The propagating gate, which answers what the trapping one cannot on the SHTns path, gives one restart hash across -finit-real=zero, -finit-real=snan with INVALID masked, and no init flag: bit identical, so nothing uninitialised reaches a stored value.

ADOPTED: config/planet.yaml no longer declares -finit-real=zero and the checked profile carries -finit-real=snan. The threaded build compiles byte for byte to c8b9c41046fd93ca, which IS the arm the 26.03% was measured on. Determinism, the one thing this could have cost, survives: verify_shtns_model.sh passes whole on the new build, both arms at rounding scale, the control rejected, four-run bit-identity giving one hash, fcf46ebbb1302d3a.

The row's premise text is also now false -- the flag line no longer carries -finit-real=zero at all.

Done. rebuild_binaries.py MATRIX now carries parmode as a fourth dimension and the build loop passes it instead of the literal "mpi"; expected() carries the _omp suffix and stays a SECOND statement of build_model.executable_name's rule so the cross-check can still fail. Per-binary provenance: each entry records parmode and its own effective_f90_opts, and the top-level toolchain records effective_f90_opts_by_parmode instead of one line, because -fopenmp -DOMPSHARED means a single global line would have repeated the exact defect toolchain() documents. assert_parmode_flags_agree() reads the flags back out of build_model.py and fails the run if the restatement drifts -- verified to fire.
